conventions.convention: The Weyl law is W(v)W(w)=exp(−iλω(v,w)/2)W(v+w), with ω((q,p),(q′,p′))=q·p′−p·q′. The Schrödinger model translates by x−q. Uniqueness assumes AC, finite dimension 2n with n≥0, a nonzero Hilbert space, λ≠0, line regularity, and irreducibility.
T(a)f(x)=f(x−a) and B_m(v)f(x)=exp(imv·x/ℏ)f(x), so the ordered loop B_m(v)T(a)B_m(v)*T(a)* has positive phase exp(imv·a/ℏ). The central-extension product has central coordinate θ+θ′−v′·a.

The boost theorem uses complex Lebesgue L² classes with inner product linear in the first argument. Its positive m and ℏ are formal mathematical parameters, without measured inputs or an asserted physical superselection law.

A_i(t)=cos(t/2)I−i sin(t/2)σ_i and D(A_i(t))′ at zero equals −iJ_i. The generator triple is irreducible and s is its largest J_z eigenvalue. Projective classes quotient by every unit scalar; ordinary descent requires D(−I)=I.

Sector restriction concerns a finite orthogonal sum of nonzero Hilbert spaces and precisely the bounded block-diagonal algebra. The trace identity applies to every trace-class ρ, without requiring positivity or normalization.

The path example explicitly identifies the product with H⊕H and uses u* w on its two-dimensional path space. Its conclusions concern squared overlaps: a loop on one arm gives cos²(θ/2), whereas a common phase on both arms gives 1.
The matrix CCR obstruction assumes positive finite matrix dimension and ℏ>0; it makes no claim about differentiating unbounded generators.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, every nonzero irreducible regular Weyl system on a finite-dimensional real symplectic space, with the displayed multiplication law and fixed λ≠0, is unitarily equivalent to the displayed Schrödinger system on L²(Rⁿ); there is exactly one such unitary-equivalence class.

Under AC and Countable Choice, for d≥1 and m,ℏ>0 the displayed translation and modulation operators are unitary and satisfy B_m(v)T(a)=exp(imv·a/ℏ)T(a)B_m(v) and B_m(v)T(a)B_m(v)*T(a)*=exp(imv·a/ℏ)I. Their displayed central extension has a strongly continuous representation Π_m and pairwise distinct central characters for pairwise distinct positive masses.

Under Countable Choice and the stated differentiability, commutator and irreducibility hypotheses, D(−I)=(−1)^(2s)I. The ray action descends continuously to SO(3); D itself descends for integer s and does not descend for half-integer s.
Under Countable Choice, for the stated finite orthogonal decomposition, every trace-class ρ and every bounded block-diagonal A satisfy tr(ρA)=tr((Σ_j P_jρP_j)A).
